name: Powerships and power barges
applications: fast capacity addition for national grids
principle: A complete engine or gas-turbine power plant is installed on a ship hull or barge, moored at a port or prepared basin and connected to the onshore grid through a switchyard, so a country adds 30 to 470 MW of capacity in weeks without land acquisition or construction. Karpowership operates the largest fleet (45 powerships, 8,500 MW installed across 20+ countries); vendors such as Power Barge Corporation and Wärtsilä deliver barge-mounted plants from 30 MW gas-turbine barges to 180 MW medium-speed-engine barges, and an estimated 75 or more power barges operate worldwide.

advantages: Capacity in weeks: no land acquisition, civil works or long construction
Relocatable when the contract ends, and financeable as moveable assets
Pairs with floating storage and regasification for LNG-to-power in gas-poor countries
limitations: Needs a suitable port or sheltered basin close to the load centre
Marine crewing, corrosion and mooring add operating cost over land-based plants
Fuel logistics (HFO, distillate or LNG) dominate operating cost; countries can become dependent on one operator
